question: Does actual cron store preserve pending job runtime responsibility across process death, reject stale definition replacement, and preserve concurrent runtime state on definition repair?
real_code: Unchanged src/cron/store.ts and transitive workspace TypeScript built with esbuild; actual Node24 built-in SQLite and Linux file IO
fixtures: Fixed job records and sequential independent OS processes. No CronService execution/model/tools. No fake DB/storage/runtime authority.

cases.input: save pending job J1(state.queuedAtMs=2000,nextRunAtMs=3000), writer exits; new process load
cases.expected: exact job configuration/runtime state retained; legacy jobs.json not authority

cases.input: load fingerprint F1; competing process changes definition; attempt saveCronJobsStore beforeWrite assertUnchanged(F1)
capture definition fingerprint; competing process updates runtime queued/running state; repair enabled=false using preserveRuntimeState=true and fingerprint guard
cases.expected: definition repair succeeds but queued/running state retained

cases.input: same store, save stale full record without preserveRuntimeState/guard
cases.expected: observe whether pending metadata lost; demonstrates caller obligation, not candidate safety support

oracle: Direct SQLite rows and fresh-process candidate load compared against fixed input fields. Source upstream store.test.ts offers API construction but assertions derive from our G1 responsibility contract.
stop: build resolves only actual needed dependencies; no replacement behavior. Candidate eachprocess30seconds. Preserve build/setup failures.
limits: Persistence of cron metadata does not prove scheduler fairness/eventual wake/exactly-once execution/runtime authorization enforcement or full gateway Session rehydration.

build_amendment.reason: cron-001 failed at module import because esbuild does not copy import.meta.url SQL resource. Build now copies unchanged source openclaw-state-schema.sql adjacent bundle. No candidate source/oracle changes.
